articles.title: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia and Korea, starting with an entertainment festival called DRX Homefront Indonesia and a joint game publishing initiative between the two countries.
body: “Indonesia is an important market for the future of entertainment in Asia,” said Can Yang, CEO of DRX. “Success in this market requires more than bringing an international brand to local audiences. It requires the right local knowledge, relationships and execution. Working with Nuon gives us the opportunity to develop experiences that reflect what Indonesian audiences want while creating stronger connections with Korea’s entertainment industry.”

The companies will explore developing DRX Homefront Indonesia as a flagship festival in Jakarta built around gaming and entertainment, drawing in players, fans and creators from both countries. Plans on the table include competitive gaming showcases, community programs for creators, fan meet-ups and concert-style shows featuring K-pop acts.

On the publishing side, the partnership will look at bringing select Korean game titles into Indonesia while helping Indonesian-developed games reach Korea. That would put DRX and Nuon in charge of everything from picking titles and adapting them for the local market to marketing, signing up players, getting the games into stores and handling payments.

articles.title: Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race
articles.summary: Hamaguchi Ryusuke’s “All of a Sudden” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan (Eiren) has revealed.
body: The film premiered in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May, where it drew a seven-minute standing ovation. Efira and Okamoto shared the festival’s best actress prize; Okamoto is the first Japanese performer to win it.
“All of a Sudden” opened in Japan on June 19 through Bitters End. Diaphana Distribution released the film in France on Aug. 12, and Neon will open it in North American theaters on Nov. 25.

Eiren’s pick now advances to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, which will winnow submissions from countries around the world down to a shortlist of 15 films before narrowing to five nominees. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place March 14, 2027.

articles.title: The Last Sunrise review – Amazon’s soapy YA romance is thankless and bland
articles.summary: Another familiar concoction fails to make use of its sunny location and chooses cheap melodrama over romantic charm. A titular sunrise, a summer fling fantasy, exorbitant wealth, impossibly sculpted bodies: such are the profitable story ingredients that make up The Last Sunrise, the latest offering…
body: Oh, right: money. In recent years, romance – which has long been maligned as an “unserious” genre – has regained prominence in the cultural spotlight. The romcom died and was reborn as steamy television; commercial romance fiction filled with graphic detail. But as the genre returns to its position as a pillar of the entertainment industry, the human-scale simplicity that gave us Bridget Jones’s Diary has been neglected and replaced by half-baked efforts like The Last Sunrise – the main value of which is to expose, all too clearly, how indifferently streaming platforms regard their audience.

articles.title: Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia
articles.summary: The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the market of the Busan International Film Festival, will present InnoAsia 2026, its program built around the intersection of film and emerging technology.
body: Beyond brands and filmmakers, InnoAsia is deepening ties with technology firms and international markets. This year’s AI-driven tech participants include AWS, Google DeepMind, BytePlus, Alibaba Cloud, Netflix’s VFX studio Eyeline Studios, MegazoneCloud, OPIM Digital, the Korean Film Archive’s VFX trading platform i.AM, Kling AI and Inshorts.

InnoAsia 2026 will run several programs across three tracks: technology proof-of-concept and investment, creators and production, and industry and policy. The InnoAsia Startup Demo Jam sits at the center of the first track, with nine companies, drawn from the open call and international partner recommendations, pitching AI, virtual production and digital-asset technologies to investors and buyers. The InnoAsia WIP Showcase will preview AI-based features, animation, series and interactive projects from directors including Pierre Zandrowicz, Mark Wachholz and Kang Yunsung, paired with a colloquium on AI production pipelines.

InnoAsia 2026 will run Oct. 10-13, at Exhibition Center 2, BEXCO in Busan, alongside the 31st Busan International Film Festival, which runs Oct. 6-15, and the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market, held Oct. 10-13.

articles.title: Hanging By a Wire review – cable car rescue documentary dangles viewers on the edge of disaster
articles.summary: The extraordinary fate of eight people trapped above a chasm in Pakistan makes for a tense, skilfully assembled survival story with unexpected flashes of comedy. Survival documentaries are a weird little genre of nonfiction film-making that recount the stories of accidents and natural catastrophes…
body: Credit is due to director Mohammed Ali Naqvi for pulling it all together adeptly, as well as to the seamless editing by William Grayson that nourishes the suspense and draws out some of the surprising moments of comedy. It’s good to have a bit of a giggle amid all the tension; we meet one heroic zip line enthusiast who brags about his amazing body as he struts around the gym he runs, looking buff but not outrageously so. The fact that he’s introduced halfway through the story lets us know he’ll survive, as will his best buddy, who has a lot less braggadocio.

articles.title: Elton John, Oprah Winfrey and Paul McCartney join tributes to Dolly Parton
articles.summary: The tributes have included artists across musical genres, fans from all generations and politicians from all spectrum sharing their love for the country icon.
body: Sir Paul McCartney, Oprah Winfrey, Taylor Swift, Beyoncé and Sir Elton John have led a wave of tributes to music icon Dolly Parton, honouring her impact across the globe.
The Beatles legend called Parton a "magnificent star", Oprah said she "brought the light" and the Rocket Man singer dubbed her a "giant of an artist" who was "irreplaceable".
Parton died on Tuesday at the age of 80, after "a brief battle with cancer", her team said in a statement to CBS, the BBC's US partner.

Tributes have poured in from US presidents across the political spectrum and musicians across all genres, remembering her not just for her award-winning career, but her philanthropy and humble nature that transcended country music.

articles.title: Practical Magic 2's Kidman and Bullock board Essex vintage train
articles.summary: The stars appear on the train, specially transported to a film studos for a new movie sequel.
body: A call from Hollywood producers asking if film stars Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock could sit in a vintage railway carriage came out of the blue for station manager Robert Bentley.
They called him to ask if the duo could use it for their new blockbuster, Practical Magic 2, a sequel to the 1998 romantic fantasy tale.
While film producers were keen to feature it, they first needed the train moved from North Weald, Essex, to the Warner Bros Studios in Leavesden, Hertfordshire.
The studio filming left Bentley "in awe", he said. "When you're stood at the studio and then all of a sudden Sandra is stood next to you, it's hard to describe the feeling."

articles.title: The Dog Stars review – Ridley Scott’s lethargic postapocalyptic drama is a misfire
articles.summary: An adaptation of Peter Heller’s 2012 novel never finds its footing with overly familiar survival beats and a glum lack of energy. Looking towards the end of an August movie dumping ground littered with more unwanted trash than usual, there seemed to be a faint glimmer of hope, a shiny treasure…
body: Hig’s belief that something more is out there causes him to leave for a nearby hub and, on the way, encounter a father-daughter pairing (Guy Pearce and Margaret Qualley) who end up joining him just as so-called “reapers” – essentially bloodthirsty goth invaders – come a’knocking.

It’s not that the action entering the fray so late into the movie is the problem here (I’m all for a more subdued character-based end-of-days drama a la Z for Zachariah ) or that the set pieces are all a little too cut-and-paste to truly excite (where the $110m budget went is a mystery). It’s that the plot and its characters are too maddeningly insubstantial to justify such human-over-spectacle storytelling.

articles.title: Chinese artist jailed over satirical Mao sculptures, say rights groups
articles.summary: The case against Gao Zhen, who was prosecuted under a law banning "slander of heroes", has been seen as an assault on artistic freedom.
body: A Chinese artist known for his satirical sculptures of Mao Zedong has been handed a maximum three-year jail term for "slandering China's heroes", according to rights groups.
A court in Hebei province had ruled on Tuesday that Gao Zhen's work "infringes upon the hero's reputation and harms public interest".
Among the 70-year-old's most famous pieces, produced with his brother Gao Qiang, is a sculpture comprising a squad of Mao-like figures holding Jesus Christ at gunpoint.

Gao has been in detention for the past two years, and the UN and many rights groups have called for him to be released. Amnesty International has called his sentencing an "assault" on artistic freedom.

articles.title: Sky U.K.’s Meghan Lyvers Discusses IP, Original Content Mix and “Increasing the Emotional Stakes”
articles.summary: The Comcast company's scripted originals exec talks about 'War,' 'The Day of the Jackal,' working with partners, championing auteurs and British stories, and that 'The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo' adaptation.
body: Plus, early this year, Sky had success with the Rafe Spall-starring Under Salt Marsh and it has unveiled an eight-episode “bold and contemporary reimagining [that] brings The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo into the present, grounded in the characters and investigative DNA of Stieg Larsson’s Millennium novels, with themes that carry heightened relevance today.”
All in all, Meghan Lyvers, managing director, scripted originals, Sky U.K., is clearly keeping busy.

The executive first joined Sky in late summer 2022 and relocated from Amsterdam to London, reporting to Cécile Frot-Coutaz, who is chief advertising and content officer at Sky and CEO of Sky Studios. Her remit has since been expanded. Lyvers previously served as senior vp and head of international co-productions and development at CBS Studios after working as a producer at Management 360. She began her career at Robert De Niro and Jane Rosenthal’s Tribeca Productions with such projects as About a Boy and the Meet the Parents franchise.
